newsitem.title: UK: Gold clings to support as silver sell-off abates.
newsitem.headline: Gold clings to support as silver sell-off abates.

text.p: Bullion clung to support at $347.00 on Friday with no fund selling in sight, but remained fragile against a renewed assault on silver, dealers said.

"At the moment gold is due for a further drop based on what happened in silver, but the market is very quiet," said one dealer. "Most people are quite happy to go home and leave it at that, but I think New York may take it lower," he added.
Gold fixed a touch higher at $347.40 versus $347.35, and stood at $347.20/$347.70 after a brief dip below the $347.00 support. It had closed at $348.40/$348.90 on Thursday.
Silver ticked up but remained exposed to fresh fund selling.
"There is various levels of support coming through but it has not really recovered too much. I think most people are still looking for a test on the downside again," said one dealer.
"We could be looking at $4.50 today or next week. If it breaks $4.50 you'll be seeing the beginning of a bloodbath."
But COMEX silver bounced, and gold received support from a rise in U.S. jobs data, although June eased $1.20 to $350.20.

But a break of $346.50 could set the bullion ready for a "hose down" to $340, dealers said, adding that, gold's direction was now tied to fund activity in silver, which slipped to its lowest level since mid-January of $4.65 in a fund raid Thursday.
Silver's inability to conquer higher territory above $5.30 frustrated funds, which had built long positions earlier this year, and more of them could be expected to liquidate.
Dealers saw critical support at around $4.55-$4.60, which, if breached could send the market sharply lower. At 1445 GMT, silver was indicated at $4.72/$4.74 from Thursday's $4.82/$4.84.
"It does look overdone but that doesn't mean they (the funds) can't come and have another go," he said.
Tumbling U.S. stock markets due to fears of higher interest rates could come into play in gold although the market has yet to see a cash influx from equities or bonds, dealers said.
"The level of buying (in gold) has been surprisingly weak and there hasn't been an awful lot of physical buying around, which is also a bit worrying," said one dealer.
Weak silver also drove platinum lower but dealers noted underlying support while there were no talks between Russia and Japan on PGM sale contracts which expired at the end of 1996.
Platinum was testing support at $361.50/$362.50, down $3.50 on the day, while palladium was $2.50 higher at $148.00/$149.00.
